dedupe_keys.name: rawclic consolidated component and material composition data for data centres

description: Researchers at Empa, the Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology, publish consolidated data on the component and material composition of data centres as Deliverable 3.1 of the EU-funded RAWCLIC project, to assess raw material demand, resource intensity and environmental footprints of the global data centre stock. Data centres are classified by facility type (cluster, colocation, enterprise, edge, HPC, hyperscale, micro), size (small, medium, large) and primary application (AI, cloud, storage, traditional, retail, wholesale). The physical structure is modelled from facility rack counts, through the shares of compute, storage, GPU and AI, and network racks, down to hardware units and their printed circuit board areas (mainboards, GPU boards, DIMMs, network cards, riser cards, power supplies, storage controllers, backplanes), each with minimum, mode and maximum values and Monte Carlo statistics. Coverage: generic global archetypes, 2026. Format and access: an Excel workbook, a PDF report with sources and quality notes, and histograms (under 2 MB) on Zenodo, free of charge under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: archetypes from literature and expert estimates, not surveyed facilities. Simulation uses: equipment stocks per data centre type for replacement and recovery planning, supply chain risk of hardware and materials, and embodied impacts. Related records: the 451 Research knowledge base and the Virginia facility dataset give facility counts to scale these archetypes.
